title: Fast transcripts that were wrong
subtitle: GPU speech recognition that was far faster than the CPU path and quietly dropped sentences, and the correctness gate every GPU integration in the voice engine now passes

stats.label: faster than the CPU path at best on the GPU, 18× at worst
workarounds in the tensor library, none of which held

lede: The voice engine recognises speech one utterance at a time: the voice-activity detector decides where a turn ends, and the whole turn goes to the recogniser in one call. On the CPU that call had a floor of about a second, because the recogniser pads every input to a thirty-second window before it listens. A second of dead air after every sentence is the difference between a colleague and a voicemail, so the recogniser moved to a server on a Blackwell GPU, and turns came back in 38 to 74 milliseconds. The transcripts looked fine in the log and were wrong in the room. Whole sentences were missing.
quote: A system can be fast and green and wrong.
evidence: Speech recognition pipelines on GPUs: recognition 18 to 25 times faster than the CPU path, with a fallback runtime at 235 ms per turn.
ML output correctness testing: a fixture comparing a known recording with its known transcript, added after a fast GPU path silently dropped whole sentences.
Root-cause analysis on new GPU toolchains: 4 workarounds in the tensor library failed and a one-line base-image change brought the dropped sentences back.
author: Corey James
